title: Black Holes as Licensed Limit Regimes
description: Separates classical black-hole geometry from the requirements of exterior reconstruction. Mass, charge, angular momentum and thermodynamic quantities retain their declared exterior roles; they do not automatically reconstruct crossed content.
source_sections: Sections 1.3, 4-6, 8-10; formalization boundary in Appendix H

title: Horizon Instability as an Admissible Reconstruction Obstruction
description: Establishes the fixed-exterior-scope no-totalization obstruction: a missing standing-transport assignment cannot be completed without an admissible witness, certificate or declared change of scope. Global storage alone is not exterior recovery.
source_sections: Sections 8, 12-15; the finite example follows Definition 14.2 and Theorem 14.4

title: Standingless Interiors and Residual Coherence
description: Classifies retained, role-indexed organization after old-scope standing loss. The horizon is not an AMetric reset, residual coherence is not annihilation, and governance-depth measures thinning successor support rather than distance or elapsed time.
source_sections: Parts II-IV, especially pages 25-29 and 35-37; main theorem on page 51

title: AMetric Normal-Form Homology
description: Derives the AMetric endpoint profile for a nonempty, unresolved residue after residual metric-support exhaustion and route closure. Origin and endpoint are distinct boundary tokens with the same role profile, without crossing or inheritance.
source_sections: Section 5, especially Theorem 5.9; Table 6 and Theorem 6.2

title: Black Holes as Constraint-Forced Origins
description: Closes the counter-boundary classification for the certified endpoint target. The unique surviving governance-equivalence class has fresh internal governed-domain status, not inherited contents, causal production or a selected populated cosmology.
source_sections: Sections 5-7, especially antecedents A1-A9 and Theorem 6.2; target-class hierarchy in Sections 10-12
